machine: one Windows 11 laptop, 12 logical CPUs; API, PostgreSQL 16 and the load generator all on it
caveat: Laptop numbers with large run-to-run variance (see load_test.variance). They show the shape of the scaling and where the ceilings are, not production capacity.

latency_light_load.what: /v1/price with a real audit row, 4 clients, 4 workers, 5 audit chains

load_test.tool: Locust 2.46, closed loop, 32 clients, 20 s per run, every request a new entity

real_prices_5_audit_chains.note: median of the runs listed; req/s

real_prices_1_audit_chain.note: every price appends to the same (tenant, domain) chain: one writer at a time

simulate_no_writes.note: engine + API only; at 8 workers the single-process load generator is probably the limit

load_test.variance: identical 4-worker runs ranged from 213 to 667 req/s; treat single numbers as rough

resilience.what: Postgres made to refuse every connection to the app database while the server was running

integrity.what: audit rows edited, removed or inserted by the database owner
integrity.not_detected_by_design: deleting the newest rows of a chain

propagation.without_redis_s: up to 10 (pack and control poll) / 60 (key cache)
